text: Assigned 2026-08-29 05:25Z. RATIONALE: the scout found, twice tonight, a defect in a direction the chief had already blessed - the population ADT stuffing and then the estimand guard on the internalRatio fix, the second of which would have shipped a bias in the opposite direction. Both were read-only, unclaimed, on modules it does not own. The internalRatio defect is almost certainly not unique: it is one instance of a general pattern where MODEL UNCERTAINTY IS SILENTLY RENDERED AS A SUBSTANTIVE FINDING ABOUT THE PARTICIPANT. SCOPE: read-only audit of the entire interview scoring surface - Scoring.scala, the phenomenology and profile strands, AiCompatibleScores, the traditional internal/external view, HardCountRule and every derived number the module publishes. For each number a reader could quote, ask three questions. (a) WHAT IS THE ESTIMAND - what quantity about the participant does this claim to measure? (b) WHERE DOES OUR OWN UNCERTAINTY GO - into the numerator, the denominator, an abstention, or silently nowhere? (c) IF UNCERTAINTY CORRELATES WITH A PARTICIPANT PROPERTY (vagueness, disorganisation, digressiveness, length), DOES THIS NUMBER MOVE IN A CONSISTENT DIRECTION? A yes to (c) is the manufactured-group-difference failure and is P1 by default. Do NOT claim paths or edit; post findings on coordination and the chief rules. Precedent to reuse: Coverage exists in this module and is integer-valued, so it cannot express fractional placement mass - check whether other strands lean on it for a job it cannot do.
